info.title: Pharmacy API
info.description: API for ordering medicines from your pharmacy network — serviceability, catalogue search and prices, estimates, orders, prescriptions and cancellation. Every call must include a valid `ls-api-key` header, and every change to an order is sent to your pharmacy webhook.

ApiKeyAuth.name: ls-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key issued by LabStack. Pass this in every request header. Your store can hold two active keys at once, so you can move to a new key before the old one is revoked. A key may have an expiry date; a request made with an expired or revoked key is refused as unauthorized.

error.example: Authorisation failed - API Key not present in HTTP Header.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized — API key missing, invalid, expired or revoked

TooManyRequests.description: Too many failed authentication attempts from your address. Every request from that address is refused, whatever key it carries, until the number of seconds in the Retry-After header has passed.

BadRequest.description: Bad request — missing or invalid parameters

post.description: Attaches prescriptions to one of your orders, by `orderId` or `referenceId`. Prefer sending them in Place Order's `documents`, where they reach the pharmacy with the order. `forwarding` says how these reach the pharmacy. WITH_ORDER - the pharmacy has not received the order yet, and the documents go with it. BY_LABSTACK - the pharmacy already has the order, so LabStack forwards the documents to it; allow time for that before the pharmacy acts on them. A CANCELLED, FULL_DELIVERED or PARTIAL_DELIVERED order takes no documents (409). When some documents are stored and others are not, the call succeeds and `errors` names the ones that were not; when none are stored it is a 503 and safe to retry.

post.description: Creates a pharmacy order for a patient and sends it to the pharmacy. The basket is checked exactly as Get Estimate checks it, and the order is created only when the pharmacy can supply every drug in the quantity asked; otherwise the call is a 400 naming the drugMasterIds, and nothing is created. Only the drugMasterIds you send are ordered - nothing is substituted. A drug marked `notForSale` in the catalogue (Schedule X or habit-forming) cannot be ordered online: a basket containing one is a 400 naming it, whatever prescriptions are sent. Prescriptions go in `documents`. They are required when any drug needs one (Get Estimate's `prescriptionRequired`), and they reach the pharmacy with the order. A document added later with Upload Prescription is forwarded by LabStack instead. If the documents cannot be stored the call is a 503, no order is left behind, and it is safe to retry. Send a `referenceId` - your own order id - to make retries safe: while an order with that referenceId exists and is not cancelled, a second Place Order with it is a 409 that returns the existing `orderId`. A request identical to one still in progress is also a 409. `order.price.totalAmount` is what the customer pays: each drug's MRP less your store's customer medicine discount, which is also what the pharmacy invoices the customer, plus `additionalCharges`. `order.price.storeTotalAmount` is what your store owes LabStack: each drug's MRP less your store's own medicine discount, plus the same `additionalCharges`. Both are fixed when the order is placed and never rise afterwards; they drop only if a drug is dispatched from a batch printed at a lower MRP, which Get Order Details then reports. A 200 means LabStack has the order; `orderStatus` says where it is. PLACED - the pharmacy has it. CREATED - taken by LabStack for a pharmacy it places orders with directly. PENDING - waiting for payment (`isPaymentRequired` is true), or the pharmacy did not accept it automatically, in which case `placementError` says so and LabStack follows it up. Every later change arrives on the Order Status Webhook. Set `isPaymentRequired` to collect payment before the order is sent. The response then carries a `paymentLink`, valid until `paymentLinkExpiresAt` (16 minutes). The order stays PENDING and the pharmacy does not see it until it is paid. Once paid it is sent and moves to PLACED - or CREATED for a pharmacy LabStack places orders with directly, or stays PENDING if the pharmacy does not accept it - and the webhook reports it. If the link lapses unpaid the order is cancelled. Payment needs a live price (Get Estimate's `canCollectPayment`), and when payment cannot be set up the call is a 503 with no order left behind. HOME_DELIVERY needs `address`, `city`, `state` and `pincode`. PICKUP needs the patient's `pincode` or a `latitude`/`longitude` pair, and is accepted only when the pharmacy's pickup point is within `range` km of it (10 unless sent, at most 100) - the rule Check Serviceability and Get Estimate apply. `pickupLocation` in the response is where the customer collects the order. One of `dateOfBirth` or `age` is required.

get.description: The full state of one of your orders, by LabStack `orderId` or by the `referenceId` you placed it with - send exactly one. `items` come back in the shape Place Order accepts - drugMasterId and quantity - with the customer price each was placed at, and the store price beside it. `unitPrice`, `subTotal` and `totalAmount` are what the customer pays: MRP less your store's customer medicine discount at the time of placing. `storeUnitPrice`, `storeSubTotal` and `storeTotalAmount` are what your store owes LabStack: MRP less your store's own medicine discount, plus the same `additionalCharges`. When the order ships, a drug dispatched from a batch printed at a lower MRP is repriced at that MRP with the same discounts, and both sets of totals drop with it; a higher printed MRP never raises a price. An order placed before customer prices were recorded reports the prices it was placed at, with no `mrp`, null store figures and possibly no `additionalCharges`. The pharmacy may split an order into several fulfilments, each with its own orderId and status. Such an order carries a `pharmaSuperOrderId` and lists the other fulfilments in `relatedOrders`. On a split, `totalAmount` and `storeTotalAmount` are for the whole order while `price` covers this fulfilment only; the delivery charge is made once, so it appears on one fulfilment. A referenceId names the fulfilment Place Order returned. A PICKUP order carries `pickupLocation`, where the customer collects it - the pharmacy's current address and opening hours. `address` stays the patient's, as sent to Place Order. Every documented field is always present; a value that does not exist is null. Order Status Webhook: every change to an order is POSTed to your store's pharmacy webhook URL, authenticated like your other LabStack webhooks. It carries `event` (what changed - orderStatus, paymentStatus, shipmentSpeed, pharmacy or drugs), `orderId`, `referenceId`, `orderStatus`, `previousStatus`, `orderType`, `orderDate`, `lsPharmacyId`, `pharmacyName`, `shipmentSpeed`, `paymentStatus`, `isPaymentRequired`, `pharmaSuperOrderId`, `shipmentTrackingId`, `totalAmount`, `cancelReason`, `uniqueId` and `userName`; call this endpoint for everything else.

post.description: Prices a basket at a pharmacy before any order exists, for partners that show a total or collect payment on their own platform. The basket is checked exactly as Place Order checks it - your network, the order type, the drugs the pharmacy lists, drugs that are not for sale, the location and the shipment speed - so a basket accepted here is accepted there unless stock or prices change in between. A basket containing a drug marked `notForSale` (Schedule X or habit-forming) is rejected with a 400 naming it. `unitPrice`, `subTotal` and `totalAmount` are what the customer pays: each drug's MRP less your store's customer medicine discount, plus `additionalCharges` - delivery and every other fee - on top. `storeUnitPrice`, `storeSubTotal` and `storeTotalAmount` are what your store owes LabStack: each drug's MRP less your store's own medicine discount, plus the same `additionalCharges`. Both totals are the figures Place Order fixes for the order if nothing changes; re-read them from Place Order's response. `allItemsAvailable` is false when the pharmacy cannot supply a drug, or not in the quantity asked; Place Order refuses that basket, and the item's `available` says which. Unavailable items are priced but left out of `subTotal` and `totalAmount`. `prescriptionRequired` is true when Place Order will need a prescription in `documents`. `canCollectPayment` is true when Place Order will accept `isPaymentRequired` for this basket. `isLivePrice` is false for a pharmacy that prices from its catalogue, whose stock is confirmed only once it receives the order. Location: send the patient's `pincode` or a `latitude`/`longitude` pair, for either order type. PICKUP is accepted on the rules Check Serviceability applies: the pharmacy's pickup point must be within `range` km of that location (10 unless sent, at most 100), or the call is a 400 giving the distance. `distance` and `pickupLocation` then say how far away the pickup point is and where the customer collects the order; both are null for HOME_DELIVERY, and for a pharmacy that chooses the pickup point when the order is placed.

post.description: Cancels one of your orders, by `orderId` or `referenceId`. An order the pharmacy has not received yet - waiting for payment, or not accepted automatically - is cancelled at once. Otherwise the pharmacy is asked, and may refuse once it has started on the order; a refusal is a 409, the order keeps its status, and LabStack follows it up with the pharmacy. Cancelling an order that is already CANCELLED succeeds and changes nothing, so a retry is safe. A FULL_DELIVERED or PARTIAL_DELIVERED order cannot be cancelled (409). For an order the pharmacy split into several fulfilments, cancelling any one cancels the whole order; `relatedOrders` reports where each of the others ended up, since a fulfilment the pharmacy had already accepted is left with it. A cancelled order's referenceId can be used again with Place Order. Money already paid through the order's payment link is owed back, and LabStack arranges the refund.

get.description: Lists the pharmacies in your network that can fulfil an order at a location, with the order types and shipment speeds each offers there. Send `pincode`, a `latitude`/`longitude` pair, or both. The optional address fields refine a pincode into a more precise location and require it. HOME_DELIVERY is offered where the pharmacy delivers to the location. PICKUP is offered when the pharmacy's pickup point is within `range` km of the location - 10 km unless you send `range`, at most 100. `distance` says how far away it is, and `pickupLocation` where the customer collects the order and when the pharmacy is open. A few pharmacies choose the pickup point nearest the customer only when the order is placed; they are listed for PICKUP with a null `distance` and `pickupLocation`, and `range` does not apply to them. Order: with `orderType=PICKUP`, the nearest pickup point comes first. Otherwise pharmacies come in your network's order of preference, the nearest first among those you prefer equally. A pharmacy with no `distance` follows those with one. Use a returned `lsPharmacyId` with Search Drugs, Get Estimate and Place Order, and send Get Estimate and Place Order the same location and `range`: they apply the same rules. A `shipmentSpeed` you send to them must be one of that pharmacy's `shipmentSpeeds`; an empty list means the pharmacy offers no choice of speed, so omit it.

get.description: Pages through the drugs your pharmacy network lists, by name. Send `query` to search by brand or salt name; omit it to page through the whole catalogue. Send `lsPharmacyId` to list one pharmacy's drugs only. Each drug is one row with its pack - `packContainer`, `packQty` and `packUnit`, which are the drug's own and the same at every pharmacy - and `pharmacies`: every network pharmacy that lists it, with its MRP there, `customerPrice` - what the customer pays, the MRP less your store's customer medicine discount - and `storePrice` - what your store owes LabStack, the MRP less your store's own medicine discount. `count` and `totalPages` count drugs, not pharmacy listings. Prices here are from the catalogue; Get Estimate gives the live price and stock for a basket. `prescriptionRequired` is true when a prescription must be sent with an order containing the drug, and also when that is not confirmed either way - treat true as "collect a prescription". Drugs that cannot be sold online - Schedule X and habit-forming drugs - are listed so their details can be shown, with `notForSale: true` and `prescriptionRequired: true`. Get Estimate and Place Order reject a basket that contains one.

get.description: One drug, in the same shape Search Drugs returns: its salt composition, whether a prescription is required, its pack, and each network pharmacy that lists it with the MRP, customer price and your store's price there, cheapest to the customer first. Send `lsPharmacyId` for one pharmacy's listing only. A drug your network does not list comes back with an empty `pharmacies`. Prices are from the catalogue and listing is not live stock; Get Estimate gives the live price and stock for a basket. A drug that cannot be sold online - a Schedule X or habit-forming drug - is returned with `notForSale: true` and `prescriptionRequired: true`, so its details can be shown; Get Estimate and Place Order reject a basket that contains it.

get.description: Other drugs with the same salt composition as `drugMasterId` - other brands and packs of the same medicine - that your pharmacy network lists, by name, in the same shape as Search Drugs. Send `lsPharmacyId` to find alternatives one pharmacy stocks, for example to replace a drug Get Estimate reports unavailable there. `drug` is the drug you asked about, with its own listings. An order is never substituted automatically: only the drugMasterIds you send to Place Order are ordered, so an alternative has to be ordered explicitly. A drug with no salt composition on record has no alternatives. An alternative with `notForSale: true` - a Schedule X or habit-forming drug - cannot be ordered online either.
